title: Junos OS Overview: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Juniper has one operating system for every router, switch and firewall. It's called Junos. And it's built in a clever, careful way.

scenes.heading: The office building
scenes.narration: Think of a big office building. The concrete and steel are one thing, and the rules and security passes are another. You can renovate a floor without shutting the building. The management office makes the decisions. The lifts and corridors move people fast.

scenes.heading: Safe changes
scenes.narration: Junos protects you from mistakes. Changes go into a draft first, called the candidate. Nothing is live until you commit. And if it goes wrong, you can roll back. First, you edit the draft candidate. Then commit makes it live. And rollback takes you to an earlier version.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three things catch people out. Junos is not like Windows, it's a purpose built system based on FreeBSD. Not every vendor separates control from forwarding, but Juniper does. And a change only takes effect after you commit.

items.right: It's a purpose-built OS based on FreeBSD

items.wrong: Every vendor splits control and forwarding
items.right: Not all do; Juniper does it by design

items.wrong: A set command takes effect immediately

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Junos is one operating system for all Juniper devices. The control plane and forwarding plane are separate. And nothing goes live until you commit. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos lab.

points.t: One OS for all Juniper devices
